label: heart100-s7
summary: The model scores heart-disease risk as an additive set of direct terms plus a gated ST-depression pathway, a peak-heart-rate gate and a small thal chain, all summed on the logit scale (training AUC 0.959). The direct terms carry most of the ranking (AUC 0.767 without them): more vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raise the typical patient's predicted risk from 38% to 98%, asymptomatic chest pain is the riskiest pain type (38% for the typical patient against 5% for typical angina), and female sex has a large negative direct weight (-1.62 per sd). The ST pathway (AUC 0.881 without it) adds risk once ST depression passes a threshold that a flat slope lowers and that low resting blood pressure raises: at 2 mm on a flat slope the typical patient's risk is 66% at 120 mm Hg and 91% at 160 mm Hg. Inside it, a gate open for every woman in training (83 of 83) and for 37 of 159 men gives back part of the women's negative direct term when they have exercise angina, high fasting sugar or ST depression: exercise angina takes the typical woman from 3% to 20% but the typical man from 38% to 31%. A high peak heart rate lowers risk above a threshold that is lower with a normal resting ECG. Worth checking: high fasting sugar has a positive direct weight on its normal level, so for a constructed typical man high sugar lowers predicted risk from 38% to 2%, although the 23 training men with high sugar get a mean predicted risk of 46% against an outcome rate of 43%. The annotated model matches the network to within 3.3e-16 on the training rows.
